papers_read.title_as_printed: Explainable machine learning models for identifying mild cognitive impairment in older patients with chronic pain (Zhang et al., BMC Nursing 2025)
Predictive model for identifying mild cognitive impairment in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A CHAID decision tree analysis (Maimaitituerxun et al., Brain and Behavior 2024)

what_each_reports.P-307: 612 chronic-pain inpatients aged >=60 (27.6% MCI by Petersen/IWG criteria incl. MoCA<26); predictors age, education, pain sites, pain duration, VAS pain, GDS-15, PSQI; 70/30 split, SMOTETomek on training; XGBoost test AUC 0.925 (95% CI 0.863-0.995); logistic regression test AUC 0.895 (0.829-0.966).
what_each_reports.P-270: Hospital-based case-control study of 1001 T2DM inpatients aged >=40 (274 MCI by Petersen criteria with education-adjusted MMSE cut-offs); predictors age, education, household income, physical activity, diabetic nephropathy, diabetic retinopathy (CHAID); 7:3 split; decision-tree AUC 0.75 (0.71-0.78) training and 0.67 (0.61-0.74) validation; logistic regression 0.76 training, 0.69 (0.62-0.75) validation.

quantity_a: Held-out AUC for identifying prevalent MCI in older (>=60) chronic-pain patients from pain, mood, sleep, age and education variables; MCI defined with MoCA<26.
quantity_b: Training (0.75) or validation (0.67) AUC for identifying prevalent MCI in T2DM inpatients aged >=40 from demographic, lifestyle and diabetic-complication variables; MCI defined with education-adjusted MMSE.
incompatible_if_same: Numerically the intervals do not overlap (P-307 test 0.863-0.995 vs P-270 validation 0.61-0.74), so if these were one quantity they would conflict. They are not: each AUC is the discrimination of a different predictor set in a different clinical population against a differently operationalised MCI label, and neither paper claims anything about the other's model or population.

gates.task: match in class (cross-sectional MCI identification from clinical/tabular data).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: two independent single-centre Chinese hospital cohorts (Nanchang pain department vs Changsha endocrinology department); record itself says dataset_equal No, and no waiver is recorded.
gates.validation_tier: match (both internal random hold-out, no external validation).
gates.modality_family: match at family level (clinical/tabular), but the predictor sets share only age and education.

endpoint_and_metric: partly compatible: both ROC-AUC for prevalent MCI, but the reference standard differs (MoCA<26 plus criteria and neurologist confirmation vs education-adjusted MMSE thresholds plus criteria) and the populations differ (chronic pain, >=60 vs T2DM, >=40, mean age 60).
performance_validity: flag not tripped (0.925 < 0.97; 184-patient test set). P-307's CI upper bound (0.995) and its SMOTETomek-balanced training make its estimate optimistic, but the automatic exclusion does not apply.
grounds: The two AUCs measure different predictor sets: P-307 uses pain intensity, depression and sleep scales, and P-270 uses income, physical activity and diabetic complications, with only age and education in common.
The populations differ (chronic-pain patients aged >=60 vs T2DM inpatients aged >=40), and so does the MCI reference standard (MoCA<26 vs education-adjusted MMSE).
The dataset-family gate fails (two unrelated hospital cohorts) with no waiver on record, and neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes.

evidence_quotes.quote: the XGBoost model performed best, achieving an accuracy of 0.883 and an AUC of 0.925 (95% CI 0.863-0.995).

record_defects: claim_b 'AUC 0.75' is P-270's training-set AUC; the held-out validation AUC is 0.67 (0.61-0.74), which is what corresponds to P-307's test-set figure.
task_equivalence true / dataset_family_equivalence true contradict dataset_equal 'No' within the same record.
apparent_performance_gap '17.5 percentage points' uses the training value; on held-out data the gap is 25.5 points, which is still not a comparison of like with like.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' rests on a generic list of ~50 'bridging' papers with no named separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A reader who treats 'clinical/tabular MCI identification in Chinese hospital patients' as one quantity and waives the dataset gate would face non-overlapping AUC intervals; the verdict would then turn on whether a difference in population and predictor set can be waived, which the rule as applied does not allow. Evidence that the same model was applied to both populations would change it.
